items.stem: Define the term 'market research'.
items.answer: The process of collecting, recording and analysing data about customers, competitors and markets.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The process of collecting, recording and analysing data about customers, competitors and markets. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of primary research.
items.answer: Advantage: the data is up to date and collected for the business's exact purpose. Disadvantage: it is expensive and time-consuming to collect.
items.markingKey: 1 mark advantage, 1 mark explanation; 1 mark disadvantage, 1 mark explanation. [4]

items.stem: Explain the difference between quantitative and qualitative research.
items.answer: Quantitative research collects numerical data, such as how many people would buy; qualitative research collects opinions and reasons, such as why people prefer a brand.
items.markingKey: 1 mark quantitative; 1 mark qualitative. [2]

items.stem: Based in Accra, Gold Coast Cocoa Ltd (private limited company) buys cocoa from local co-operatives and makes premium chocolate bars. The business has around 450 employees. World cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months. Explain the market research methods Gold Coast Cocoa could use before launching cocoa-based beauty products.
items.answer: Points to develop for Gold Coast Cocoa: market research reduces the risk of a new product; secondary research on market size and competitors; primary research such as surveys and focus groups; test marketing in one area.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: market research reduces the risk of a new product. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Gold Coast Cocoa (confectionery). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. secondary research on market size and competitors; primary research such as surveys and focus groups. [3]

items.stem: Savanna Fresh Ltd is a private limited company based in Nairobi, Kenya. It grows cut flowers and green beans and exports them by air to supermarkets in Europe and employs about 850 people. Its largest European customer has just demanded lower prices and proof of sustainable water use. Explain the advantages to Savanna Fresh of using secondary research about the Gulf states.
items.answer: Points to develop for Savanna Fresh: secondary research uses existing data; cheap and quick to obtain; gives market size and trends in the Gulf states; helps plan primary research.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: secondary research uses existing data. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Savanna Fresh (horticulture). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. cheap and quick to obtain; gives market size and trends in the Gulf states. [3]

items.stem: Gold Coast Cocoa is a private limited company in Accra, Ghana with about 450 staff. It buys cocoa from local co-operatives and makes premium chocolate bars. World cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months. Evaluate whether Gold Coast Cocoa should use primary research or secondary research before entering the United Kingdom.
items.answer: For: primary is specific and up to date; secondary is cheap and quick; secondary gives an overview of the market. Judgement: for Gold Coast Cocoa it depends mainly on the budget, and also on how different the United Kingdom is.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Gold Coast Cocoa. [10]

items.stem: Define the term 'sample'.
items.answer: A group of people chosen from the target population to take part in market research.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – A group of people chosen from the target population to take part in market research. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why businesses use samples rather than asking the whole population.
items.answer: Asking everyone would be too expensive and take too long; a representative sample gives reasonably accurate results at a much lower cost.
items.markingKey: 1 mark cost/time; 1 mark representative sample gives accurate enough results. [2]

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of quota sampling.
items.answer: Advantage: it is quick and ensures each group is represented. Disadvantage: interviewers choose who to ask, which can introduce bias.
items.markingKey: 1 mark advantage, 1 mark explanation; 1 mark disadvantage, 1 mark explanation. [4]

items.answer: Points to develop for Hamid Engineering: sampling methods differ in cost and bias; random sampling avoids selection bias; quota sampling is quick and represents key groups; sample size affects reliability and cost.

items.stem: Define the term 'mean'.
items.answer: The arithmetic average: the sum of the values divided by the number of values.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The arithmetic average: the sum of the values divided by the number of values. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why the mean may be misleading when a set of data contains an extreme value.
items.answer: The mean includes every value, so one very high or low value pulls it away from the typical value; the median would better represent the data.
items.markingKey: 1 mark extreme value distorts mean; 1 mark median better. [2]

items.stem: Explain why a business might present market research data in charts rather than tables.
items.answer: Charts make patterns and comparisons easier to see quickly, helping managers understand results and communicate them to others.
items.markingKey: 1 mark easier to see patterns; 1 mark aids decisions/communication. [2]

items.answer: Points to develop for Iberia Moda: averages show a typical value; the mean uses all data but is affected by extremes; the median and mode are less affected; the range shows the spread of views.

items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'mode'?

items.stem: Define the term 'reliability (of research)'.
items.answer: The extent to which market research results are accurate and would be the same if the research were repeated.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The extent to which market research results are accurate and would be the same if the research were repeated. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain two reasons why market research results may be unreliable.
items.answer: The sample may be too small or biased, so it does not represent the market; and respondents may not answer honestly or may change their minds.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark reason, 1 mark explanation): sample, question design, dishonest answers, out-of-date data, researcher bias. [4]

items.stem: Explain why a small business might decide that extensive market research is not cost-effective.
items.answer: The cost of research may be large relative to its budget and the size of the decision, and the owner's knowledge of local customers may be good enough.
